Martin, N., Worrell, E., Ruth, M., Price, L. (LBNL), Elliott, R.N., Shipley, A.M. and Thorne, J. (ACEEE) (2000). Emerging Energy-Efficient Industrial Technologies. Report LBNL-46990, Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, October 2000. No DOI printed.

Region: United States (2015 market base case). Locators are printed page numbers of the Section VI data tables (PDF page offset not checked; the page numbers are those printed at the foot of each profile data table, one profile spanning the pages before it). Main file: the 55 technology data tables of Section VI (54 profiles of Table ES-1 plus the Hi-Tech HVAC table): one new-measure example per technology with description, state-of-development, year-available, lifetime; for the 31 profiles whose energy figures are per short ton (or tonne, barrel) of product: electricity and fuel per unit of product for the new measure and, where the reference technology has an archetype-like identity, a second example for the reference technology; capex (investment per unit of annual capacity) and opex-total (change in annual O&M/other costs per unit relative to the reference, negative = saving). Costs have no price year (PRICE YEAR NOT STATED; 2000 used) and are mostly incremental to the reference. The four power-equipment profiles (CHP turbine, reciprocating engine, fuel cell, microturbine) carry efficiency, capacity and $/kW from the table and text. Profiles with sector-total or non-product bases (food heat recovery, food membranes, cooling, chemical heat exchangers, pinch analysis, process control, burners, motor systems, lighting, HVAC, wastewater, mining, textile) have only description/status/lifetime in the main file; their energy and cost numbers are in other-values and measures. _measures.csv: one row per profile with the printed saving (absolute, as printed), investment and payback. Not loaded: primary-energy numbers (other-values), 2015 market potentials (other-values), section II-V text and Tables ES-1 and ES-2 (qualitative ratings). Traps: Steel-3 printed electricity saving (436 kWh/ton, 100 %) equals the reference use, not 436-240 = 196 kWh/ton; Chem-1 electricity values (0.000056 and 0.00012 kWh/ton) are unit errors and were not loaded; Refin-1, Refin-2 and Electron-1 costs are absolute project figures with no clear per-unit basis (capex/opex left out of the main file, kept in _measures.csv); the data table figures are the analyst assumptions for a typical application, not measurements; Steel-4 savings percentage column (90 %) is wrong (0.7/2.2 MBtu = 32 %); Steel-4 and Paper-7 tables have garbled letter-spacing in the PDF text; Chem-6 reference description is a copy of Chem-5 (isopropyl/water) but its energy values (528 kWh, 14.6 MBtu per ton) look like pyrolysis; Paper-1 reference and new electricity are consumption, with power production of 800-850 kWh/ton (reference) and 1200-3000 kWh/ton (BLGCC) in the notes; Alum-2 and Alum-4 report MWh per tonne, others kWh per short ton; investment costs for Alum-2 were converted at CAD 1.2 per USD by the source; Motorsys and lighting values are per motor, per fixture or per 100 cfm, not per product; Steel-5 and Steel-3/-1 unit costs are per ton of annual capacity; heating-value basis is not stated for any fuel number; the table data for Food-2, Food-3, Food-4, Chem-3, Other-2, Other-4 and Other-5 are sector totals (TWh, TBtu).
